summary: Inflight request preemption by priority rebalancer causing elevated 5xx rate
description:
Issue summary:
We observed a sustained increase in 5xx responses for customer Vernon Analytics (dedicated tenant) originating from api-gateway and upstream serving-runtime restarts. Error rate spike started 2026-03-13 14:12 UTC and correlated with an automated priority rebalancing job executing across the ingress-prioritizer fleet.

Impact:
- ~12% of requests for the tenant returned 5xx over a 22-minute window; clients reported failing streaming sessions and aborted generation jobs.
- Customer reported production degradation for a data-processing pipeline (affects business analytics dashboards).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: prod us-east-1 (tenant pinned to a subset of GPU nodes).
- Components involved: api-gateway -> ingress-prioritizer -> serving-runtime pool (cuda nodes).

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Priority rebalancer runs and recalculates per-tenant priority buckets based on recent QPS and SLA weights.
2) In-flight lower-priority requests are preemptively evicted to rebalance capacity.
3) Evicted clients retry immediately (no jitter) causing a rapid burst against api-gateway.
4) Api-gateway queues spike, backpressure increases, and several serving runtime workers exceed allowed KV cache thrash limits leading to watchdog restarts and OOM-like termination (SIGABRT).
5) Subsequent requests receive 502/503/504 depending on proxy path and timing.

Observed behavior & logs (selected):
- apigw logs (us-east-1, 2026-03-13 14:12:30 - 14:34:00): repeated upstream 502s; connection resets followed by 429s at the gateway when token buckets hit zero. Link: https://dash.redwood.com/apigw/errors?svc=us-east-1&window=2026-03-13T14:10:00Z_2026-03-13T14:40:00Z
- ingress-prioritizer: job "rebalance-cycle-2026-03-13-14:11" completed in 18s. Logs show mass eviction events for tenant id t-vernon-11 with reason PREEMPTIVE_REBALANCE.
- serving-runtime: repeated worker watchdog restarts with stack traces indicating rapid KV cache invalidation and repeated memory pressure before abort: "runtime: aborting worker due to kv-evict-loop". Kernel-level OOMs were not recorded, but process exit codes were non-zero.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis A: Preemptive eviction without backoff caused retry amplification; retries hit the gateway burst limit and queue saturation triggered upstream timeouts.
- Hypothesis B: The rebalancer's immediate eviction approach did not signal the runtime to gracefully finish in-flight streams, causing partial state corruption of runtime's KV caches and subsequent instability when those requests retried.
- Correlated metrics: request retry rate increased 6x immediately after rebalance completion; average per-request queue time at apigw jumped from 12ms to 420ms.
- Cross-checks: No infra-level node interruptions recorded in cloud provider metrics; node CPU/GPU utilization increased but did not show sustained saturation prior to restarts.

Temporary mitigation performed (timeline):
- 14:25 UTC: Support escalated to SRE and Engineering.
- 14:32 UTC: Rolled back automated priority rebalancer for the us-east-1 ingress-prioritizer cluster to stop further evictions (hotfix toggle).
- 14:40 UTC: Applied short-term gateway rate-smoothing for tenant t-vernon-11 via dynamic token-bucket increase to allow graceful retries with jitter.
- 14:55 UTC: Performed rolling restart of 6 serving-runtime workers handling the tenant to clear the kv-cache thrash cycles; error rate began to fall.
- 15:10 UTC: Error rate returned to baseline for the tenant; monitoring shows stabilized queue times and reduced restart frequency.

Customer communication:
- CS notified customer at 14:36 UTC; provided update at 15:20 UTC confirming mitigation and next steps. Customer accepted working-with-engineering for root cause follow-up.

Next steps / recommended permanent fixes:
1) Add a grace-window in the priority rebalancer that avoids preemptive eviction of actively streaming sessions for X seconds and instead marks for low-priority tail-preemption.
2) Implement client-visible retry-jitter guidance and server-side retry token smoothing when eviction events are emitted.
3) Add a safety-check in ingress-prioritizer to not evict more than N% of in-flight requests within a single cycle.
4) Enhance runtime KV cache eviction metrics and add an automated alert when eviction storms correlate to worker restarts.
5) Postmortem & runbook update: record exact mitigation toggles and make hotfix toggle accessible to on-call without engineer approval.

Work items created:
- github.com/redwood/ingress-prioritizer/pull/129 (smoothing + grace window)
- ENG-TASK-1122: telemetry for kv eviction spikes and runtime restarts
- DOCS: update runbook confluence.redwood.com/KB/priority-rebalancer-runbook with emergency toggle steps

Resolution notes (so far):
- Root cause appears tied to the rebalancer eviction policy interacting poorly with streaming workloads and runtime cache behavior. Hotfix rollback and smoothing mitigations reduced customer impact; engineering will deploy a targeted code change to ingress-prioritizer to enforce eviction rate limits and grace periods.
